title: Chapter 3 – The Role of the Arbiter: Mock Exam

questions.text: What is the primary duty of a FIDE Arbiter?

options.text: To assist players with their moves
To see that the Laws of Chess are strictly observed
To record all moves of each game
To broadcast the games to spectators

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.1, the arbiter shall see that the Laws of Chess are strictly observed, act in the best interest of the competition, and ensure a good playing environment.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a valid penalty an arbiter can apply?

options.text: Warning the player
Declaring the game lost by the offending player
Awarding the offending player extra time
Expulsion from the event

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.2, the arbiter can increase the remaining time of the OPPONENT (not the offender). Valid penalties are: warning, increasing opponent's time, reducing offender's time, declaring loss, or expulsion.

questions.text: What should the arbiter do regarding spectators in the playing area?

options.text: Allow spectators to analyse games freely
Ensure spectators do not disturb players and may expel offenders
Permit spectators to speak with players during their turn
Invite spectators to assist with scorekeeping

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.3, the arbiter shall ensure spectators do not disturb the players. No analysis is permitted in the playing area, and the arbiter may expel offenders from the playing venue.

questions.text: When should the arbiter intervene in a game?

options.text: Whenever the arbiter believes a player is making a bad move
Only in cases described by the Laws of Chess
Whenever a player requests advice
At the end of every 10 moves

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.7, the arbiter shall not intervene in a game except in cases described by the Laws of Chess. Players must not speak to the arbiter except to make a claim.

questions.text: Who is responsible for pairings in a Swiss tournament?

options.text: The tournament organiser
The players themselves
The arbiter
FIDE headquarters

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.4, the arbiter is responsible for pairings in a Swiss or round-robin tournament and must ensure the pairing system complies with FIDE regulations.

questions.text: What is the arbiter's responsibility regarding scoresheets?

options.text: Scoresheets are the players' personal property
The arbiter collects scoresheets at end of each round and can request them during a game
Scoresheets are only needed if a dispute arises after the tournament
The arbiter writes the moves on behalf of both players

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.5, the arbiter collects scoresheets at the end of each round. They are an important piece of evidence in disputes and the arbiter can request a player's scoresheet at any time during the game.
